sections.heading: Section 1: Fundamental Counting and Linear Permutations

questions.q: In how many ways can $5$ different books be arranged on a shelf?
Evaluate the number of permutations of $7$ distinct items taken $3$ at a time, ${}^7 P_3$.
How many $4$-digit even numbers can be formed using digits $\{1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8\}$ without repetition?
questions.answer: Last digit must be 2 or 8 ($2$ choices). First three digits from remaining 5 digits: ${}^5 P_3 = 60$. Total $= 60 \times 2 = 120$.

sections.heading: Section 2: Permutations with Repetitions and Identical Items

questions.q: Find the number of distinct permutations of all the letters in the word $\text{PARALLEL}$.
questions.answer: 8 letters total: 3 L's, 2 A's, 1 P, 1 R, 1 E. Total $= \frac{8!}{3! 2!} = \frac{40320}{12} = 3360$.

questions.q: How many 6-letter arrangements of $\text{PEPPER}$ begin with the letter $\text{P}$?
questions.answer: Fix one P first. Remaining 5 letters: 2 P's, 2 E's, 1 R. Arrangements $= \frac{5!}{2! 2!} = \frac{120}{4} = 30$.

questions.q: How many 5-digit codes can be formed from digits $\{3, 3, 3, 7, 7\}$?
A committee of $4$ is to be chosen from $9$ people. How many distinct committees can be formed?
A team of $5$ is selected from $6$ boys and $4$ girls. How many teams contain exactly $3$ boys and $2$ girls?
From $10$ points on a plane where no three are collinear, how many distinct triangles can be drawn?
In how many ways can $4$ boys and $3$ girls sit in a row if all $3$ girls must sit together?
questions.answer: Treat 3 girls as 1 block. Total units: 4 boys + 1 block = 5 units ($5! = 120$). Girls within block: $3! = 6$. Total $= 120 \times 6 = 720$.

questions.q: In how many ways can $5$ people sit around a circular dinner table?
A committee of $4$ is selected from $5$ men and $5$ women. How many committees contain at least one woman?
questions.answer: Total selections $= \binom{10}{4} = 210$. All-men selections $= \binom{5}{4} = 5$. At least one woman $= 210 - 5 = 205$.
